noah.why: GEN 6:22, 7:7, 8:18 state it; the range is the whole Flood narrative but that is the event.

abram.why: 22:13 has Abraham find the ram; God's providing is stated in 22:8 and 22:14, both in range.

moses.why: The only cited verse for the leading out (EXO 12:51) says the LORD brought Israel out, and 14:21-31 credits the LORD with the sea; ACT 7:36 says Moses brought them out with signs in the Red sea.

elijah.why: Elijah prayed (18:36-37) and 'the fire of the LORD fell' (18:38); 'called down' credits him with the act, as 'healed' would where God healed.
elijah.fix_en: prayed on Mount Carmel, and the fire of the LORD fell on the sacrifice
elijah.fix_uk: помолився на горі Кармел, і Господній вогонь упав на жертву

elisha.why: 2KI 2:15 is the sons of the prophets saying it; acceptable.
Elisha prayed and stretched himself on the child (4:33-35); the text does not attribute the raising to anyone else.

simon.why: Pentecost is named only in ACT 2:1, outside the cited range.

saul-2.why: The Ukrainian makes Paul the one who met Jesus; the English (and ACT 9:17, 'Jesus, that appeared unto thee') has Jesus as the actor.
saul-2.fix_uk: на дорозі до Дамаску йому з'явився Ісус, і він охрестився

saul-2.why: ACT 13:46-49 is one city (Antioch in Pisidia); 'in many cities' needs a verse such as ACT 15:36, 'every city where we have preached'.

joseph.why: 45:4-11 is Joseph's plan to nourish them ('there will I nourish thee'); that he did keep them alive is stated in 47:12, outside the range.

samuel-2.why: 10:1 says 'captain over his inheritance', but the kingship is plain from 10:24 and 15:1; 1SA 15:1 could be added.

solomon.why: 1KI 6 never names Jerusalem; 2CH 3:1 ('the house of the LORD at Jerusalem') could be added, but the place is not in doubt.

enoch-2.why: JUD 1:14 names 'Enoch, the seventh from Adam', so it is this Enoch.

gideon.why: The English holds (7:7, 7:20-22), but the Ukrainian numeral phrase does not agree: in the instrumental the noun follows the numeral, so it is «трьомастами чоловіками», not «трьомастами чоловік».

deborah-2.why: 4:9-10 has her go up with Barak and 4:14 has her at Tabor sending him down; 'went with him to battle' is fair.

nehemiah.why: NEH 2:1-8 says only 'the city of my fathers' sepulchres' in Judah; Jerusalem is named in 1:3 and 2:11, either of which could be added.

hezekiah.why: 20:1-6 is only God's promise ('I will heal thee'); the recovery itself is 20:7.

josiah.why: Josiah ordered the repair (22:3-6); that counts as his act.
'Idols' are named in 2KI 23:24 ('the images, and the idols ... did Josiah put away'), outside 23:4-20.
«загинув від фараона» is not natural Ukrainian; the death needs «від руки».
josiah.fix_uk: загинув від руки фараона Нехо в Меґіддо

martha.why: «прийняла ... у своєму домі» does not render 'received into her house', and «клопоталася про багато служіння» is not natural Ukrainian.
martha.fix_uk: прийняла Ісуса до свого дому й клопоталася великою службою

_notes.moses: His call at the burning bush (EXO 3) and the confrontation with Pharaoh are missing; either is more central than his death (clause 3).
_notes.david: His sin with Bathsheba and the death of Uriah (2SA 11-12) is a defining event and is missing; Samuel's anointing of him (1SA 16:13) is another.
_notes.samuel-2: That he judged Israel all his life (1SA 7:15) is his chief role and is missing.
_notes.abram: Clause 2 could carry GEN 15:6 ('he believed ... counted it to him for righteousness'), which is the verse the NT quotes.
_notes.stephen: His speech before the council (ACT 7:2-53) is what most of his story consists of.
_notes.josiah: His Passover (2KI 23:21-23) is a further candidate, but the selection is sound.
_notes.deborah-2: Fine; a reader may note that Jael, not Deborah or Barak, killed Sisera (4:21).
